claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

test_case.agent_script:
=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are asking about Child Benefit for 1 child:
  - Alex is 8 years old and does not live with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Claimant contributes £26.05/week towards child's upkeep and no other claimaint has priority
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to understand your situation. 

**Do you have a child or children you're claiming for?** If so, could you tell me:
- How many children you have
- Their names and ages

This will help me determine which eligibility pathway applies to your situation. Child Benefit eligibility depends on the child's age and, in some cases, whether they're in approved education or training.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes - I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. Let me assess eligibility for Alex, who is 8 years old.

Since Alex is under 16, he falls into the automatic qualification age category. Let me check the next step.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now, **is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work)?**

Since he's only 8 years old, I would expect he's not in paid work at all, but I need to confirm this to proceed with the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work at all - he's just 8!

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Of course! That makes perfect sense. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Next question: **Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right** (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?

In other words, does Alex receive any benefits like ESA or Universal Credit in his own name?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me continue.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Next: **Is Alex in any type of apprenticeship program?**

This includes apprenticeships in England, Scotland, or Wales. Given that he's 8 years old, I expect the answer is no, but I need to confirm this.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - he's only 8, he's still in primary school!

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Absolutely right! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status. **Do you meet the UK residency requirements?**

You'll meet these requirements if **ANY** of the following applies to you:

1. **You normally live in the UK**, or
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or
3. You have pre-settled status and are working (earning above the National Insurance threshold), or
4. You have pre-settled status and are actively seeking work (for up to 91 days), or
5. You have pre-settled status with sufficient financial resources and not claiming certain benefits, or
6. You have pre-settled status as a student with sufficient resources, or
7. You have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA/Swiss national with right to reside, or
8. You're a Crown servant living abroad

**Which of these applies to your situation?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since you normally live in the UK, you meet the residency requirements. Let me continue.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check: **Are you responsible for Alex?**

You're considered responsible if **ANY** of the following applies:

1. **You live with Alex**, or
2. You contribute to Alex's upkeep (paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit would be - through things like food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents), or
3. You pay maintenance for Alex under a court order or agreement

**Which of these applies to you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me, but I do help out financially - I contribute towards his upkeep with things like clothes and other bits.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. To confirm you meet the responsibility requirement through financial contributions, I need to check: 

**Do you contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit would be towards Alex's care?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
The current Child Benefit rates are:
- **£25.60 per week** for the eldest or only child
- **£16.95 per week** for additional children

So for Alex, if he's your only or eldest child you're claiming for, the threshold would be around **£25.60 per week** (about **£110 per month**).

Your contributions can include:
- Clothes
- Food
- Pocket money
- Housing costs
- Presents
- Other costs towards his care

These can be paid weekly, monthly, or as lump sum payments.

**Do your contributions towards Alex's care add up to at least this amount (approximately £110 per month or £25.60 per week)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I contribute about £26 a week towards his upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since you contribute at least £26 per week towards Alex's upkeep, you meet the responsibility requirement. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check: **Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

This could be Alex's other parent, a guardian, or another person who cares for him.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to understand Alex's living situation. **Which of the following applies to Alex?**

1. He is currently in hospital
2. He is in local authority care
3. He is in a foster care arrangement
4. He is living normally (not in hospital, care, or foster placement)

**Which one describes Alex's situation?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's living normally - none of those special situations apply.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me continue.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Final question: **Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, is the local council paying for Alex's living costs or care?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards his care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News - You Are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit!

**For Alex (age 8): ELIGIBLE**

You meet all the Child Benefit eligibility requirements:

✅ Alex is under 16 years old  
✅ He's not in paid work  
✅ He doesn't receive benefits in his own right  
✅ You meet UK residency requirements (living in Manchester)  
✅ You're responsible for Alex through your financial contributions (£26/week)  
✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him  
✅ Alex is living normally  
✅ The local council isn't paying for his care  

---

## Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Payment**: Child Benefit is paid every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

---

## Important Information:

**Current Child Benefit Rate for Alex:**
- As your only/eldest child: **£25.60 per week** (approximately £110 per month)

**High Income Child Benefit Charge:**  
Be aware that if you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, the High Income Child Benefit Charge applies. This doesn't affect your eligibility, but you may need to pay back some or all of the Child Benefit through your tax return.

---

**Ready to apply?** Visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Do you have any questions about the application process?

All eligibility criteria are met.
